description: Drive the real Claude Code CLI against the local model double on a default install (.claude/commands/pan/), and check that none of PAN's commands is listed to the model.
why: Market-ideas M49 (MI-132, 2026-10-20): PAN's commands are invoked explicitly, so a skill description Claude Code lists to the model is context spent on every turn, and an invitation to run a PAN command unasked. `disable-model-invocation: true` on the installed command files (and on the SKILL.md a --unified-skills install mirrors; see skill-listing-claude) is meant to keep them out. MI-022 applies: a frontmatter field is emitted only once the host is seen to honour it, and this scenario is that observation. The double answers from a script, so nothing is spent.

steps.why: One turn, so the host sends its full system prompt and tool list.
No PAN skill description reaches the model: the host honours disable-model-invocation on PAN's skills.
The user types the command, as PAN's docs tell them to.

args: Display the complete PAN command reference.
steps.why: The command still runs when the user types it: its body reaches the model. disable-model-invocation only takes it out of the listing.

write.content:
---
name: pan:help
description: Show available PAN commands and usage guide
---

<objective>
Display the complete PAN command reference.
</objective>

controls.why: The same help entry without disable-model-invocation (description and body as shipped) must show up in the listing, and the listing step alone must turn the scenario red.
